upload_deadlock.before: Fails with 0 pending reads, 4 finished reads and a free writer queue.
upload_deadlock.after: Both upload queues drain within five seconds; ten consecutive targeted runs pass.

udp_trackers.before: The working torrent cannot announce within one second while another tracker is silent.
udp_trackers.after: IPv6 tracker responds within one second while IPv4 tracker drops its initial connect; the IPv4 request is retransmitted unchanged after 15 seconds and succeeds.

inbound_burst.setup: Five rounds of four concurrent handshakes from distinct loopback IPs, respecting the per-IP handshake limit.
inbound_burst.after: All four admitted peer slots attach in every round.
inbound_burst.limitation: The test also passed before increasing the route queue; it validates burst admission but does not deterministically reproduce the one-slot race.

duplicate_identity.before: Two connections remain established to the same remote peer ID.
duplicate_identity.after: Only the deterministically preferred direction survives for both peer-ID orderings. The survivor downloads both pieces and reaches seeding.

notes: pending_command and incoming receive are gated while pending_hash or pending_read is occupied.
A pending hash can stall the FIFO, but no overwrite was demonstrated. Upload reads bypassing hash ordering was not implemented.
The large-piece run below validates the current path, not a before/after performance improvement.

large_piece_silent_tracker_scale.harness_correction: Initial run stopped when its no-error assertion encountered the expected tracker timeout in last_error. The rerun permits only a tracker-reported timeout on a still-downloading or seeding torrent.

notes: Runs were sequential on the same dev machine, without dropping filesystem caches.
Measured timings are observations, not performance guarantees.
Many-file limits and long-duration soak scenarios were not run.
